item.title: JSB endorses consultation report, Bougainville referendum vote heads to National Parliament on August 27
item.description: The Joint Supervisory Body has formally endorsed the Post-Consultation Report and the Melanesian Agreement in Port Moresby today, clearing the path for the Bougainville referendum results to be tabled in the National Parliament on August 27. Co-chaired by Prime Minister James Marape and Autonomous Bougainville Government President Ishmael Toroama, the special meeting marked the official conclusion
item.content:encoded:
The Joint Supervisory Body has formally endorsed the Post-Consultation Report and the Melanesian Agreement in Port Moresby today, clearing the path for the Bougainville referendum results to be tabled in the National Parliament on August 27.

Co-chaired by Prime Minister James Marape and Autonomous Bougainville Government President Ishmael Toroama, the special meeting marked the official conclusion of post-referendum negotiations following the historic 2019 vote, where 97.7 per cent of Bougainvilleans voted for independence.

Under the agreed framework, the referendum outcome will be presented to the floor of Parliament for formal debate, with both leaders set to jointly determine the specific date for the decisive vote.

Addressing media following the closed-door session, Prime Minister Marape commended the resilience and patience of the people of Bougainville as both governments navigate the final constitutional stage of the peace process.

"This marks an important journey," Marape said. "The JSB we are having this morning is historic before we bring to rest the 97.7 per cent results of the referendum.

"Peace in 2001 was a construct of leadership from both sides as we tried to rest the civil crisis and move toward a future that is amicable. Section 342 of our Constitution clearly says Parliament will make this decision, and whatever that decision is, we must respect the parliamentary process."

However, President Toroama delivered a direct and uncompromising message to the National Government, rejecting any administrative or legal maneuvers aimed at dismissing the independence vote or reverting Bougainville to an extended autonomy model.

Toroama said the National Government’s potential non-affirming decision position was a dangerous legal fiction, and warned against treating Bougainville’s political future as a corporate performance review or political charity.

"Bougainville is moving away from the autonomy space, and let me make that clear," he said. "The question has been asked, answered, and sealed in ink and blood. We do not need a pathway to revisit that question.

"Any attempt by the National Parliament to vote down the referendum result, freeze us in a dead autonomy framework, or demand constitutional amendments is a rejection of the peace process itself."

The ABG President also voiced strong opposition to the unilateral introduction of a three-quarters voting threshold in the National Parliament, stating that the rule was established without the mandatory joint consultations required under the Melanesian Agreement.

Despite the sharp tensions over parliamentary procedure, both leaders reaffirmed their commitment to the overarching spirit of the 2001 Bougainville Peace Agreement, emphasizing that the ongoing diplomatic oversight of the United Nations remains vital to ensuring international credibility as the transition reaches its climax.

item.title: New police fleet to strengthen operations across Northern Command
item.description: Police in Morobe, Madang and Eastern Highlands are set to benefit from a new fleet of vehicles under the Royal Papua New Guinea Constabulary's fleet replacement program. The initiative is aimed at improving police mobility, reducing reliance on hired vehicles and strengthening frontline policing across the Northern Command.
item.content:encoded:
Police in Morobe, Madang and Eastern Highlands are set to benefit from a new fleet of vehicles under the Royal Papua New Guinea Constabulary's fleet replacement program.

The initiative is aimed at improving police mobility, reducing reliance on hired vehicles and strengthening frontline policing across the Northern Command.

Acting Assistant Commissioner of Police for Logistics, Chief Superintendent Christopher Smith, said the Constabulary is replacing ageing vehicles with government-owned fleet to improve operational capacity nationwide.

He said the Northern Command, which covers Morobe, Madang and Eastern Highlands, has experienced transport challenges that have affected police operations and emergency response.

Smith said reducing the use of hired vehicles would allow funds to be redirected towards other policing priorities, including operational resources and service delivery.

The new vehicles would provide officers with reliable transport to carry out patrols, respond to emergencies and deliver policing services more effectively.

Smith said the fleet replacement program forms part of broader efforts under the Special Police Assistance Program [SPAP], which is supporting improvements to police infrastructure, equipment and logistics across the country.

He said the program is designed to ensure police commands have the resources needed to perform their duties efficiently and better serve communities.

Smith also stressed the importance of proper vehicle maintenance and accountability as the Constabulary continues to expand its fleet.

The new vehicles are expected to improve response times and strengthen law and order operations across Morobe, Madang and Eastern Highlands, while supporting police officers serving communities throughout the Northern Command.

item.title: El Niño and strong winds damage food gardens, disrupt water supply in Markham
item.description: Residents of Ragiampun village in Morobe's Markham district are facing growing hardship as El Niño conditions and strong winds continue to damage food gardens and reduce water supplies. This has been a concern for both the community and nearby schools.
item.content:encoded:
Residents of Ragiampun village in Morobe's Markham district are facing growing hardship as El Niño conditions and strong winds continue to damage food gardens and reduce water supplies.

This has been a concern for both the community and nearby schools.

Strong winds have destroyed large numbers of banana trees and damaged other food crops, including taro and sweet potato, leaving many families worried about their food security and income.

The affected gardens are the main source of food and cash income for many households in the community.

Locals said the damage has come at a time when families are relying heavily on their gardens to feed their households, but prolonged dry weather and strong winds have continued to destroy crops.

The dry conditions have also reduced the community's water supply, with creeks and other water sources running low.

The water shortage is affecting both Ragiampun SDA Primary and Adventist High School, where students and teachers are struggling to access enough water for drinking, cooking, washing and other daily needs.

Ward Councillor Kelvin Sauri said the destruction of food gardens and the shortage of water were placing significant pressure on the community.

"The strong winds have destroyed our banana crops, and our water sources are drying up," he said.

"Both of our schools urgently need water. If the water supply is not restored soon, the schools could be forced to close because water is essential for students and teachers."

Community members are calling on local leaders and the Markham district administration to urgently address water supply and assist families whose food gardens have been damaged.

They said the situation indicates the need for more reliable and resilient water infrastructure to support rural communities during El Niño and other extreme weather events.

item.title: RPNGC begins 2027 election prep
item.description: The Royal Papua New Guinea Constabulary [RPNGC] has commenced early preparations for the 2027 National General Elections, focusing on resource allocation, manpower, and logistical requirements nationwide. Acting Assistant Commissioner of Police [Logistics] Christopher Smith said Police headquarters is working closely with provincial police commands to identify operational needs, including vehicles
item.content:encoded:
The Royal Papua New Guinea Constabulary [RPNGC] has commenced early preparations for the 2027 National General Elections, focusing on resource allocation, manpower, and logistical requirements nationwide.

Acting Assistant Commissioner of Police [Logistics] Christopher Smith said Police headquarters is working closely with provincial police commands to identify operational needs, including vehicles, equipment, and personnel deployments.

Smith said early planning will allow the constabulary to better prepare for the massive nationwide operation and ensure officers on the ground are adequately supported.

“Logistics will play a critical role in election security, with reliable transport, communications equipment, and other operational resources needed to support police deployments throughout the country,” Smith said.

He said key lessons learned from previous national elections are shaping strategy for 2027, with an emphasis on coordination and operational readiness.

Smith said continued backing from the National Government and key development partners will be crucial to securing the necessary resources to maintain law and order throughout the election period.

Planning will continue over the coming months as provincial commands submit their requirements to headquarters.

item.title: Power restoration underway at Magarima Station
item.description: Electricity is set to be restored at Magarima Station in the Magarima District of Hela Province, with major work now underway to install two new 500 kilowatt generators. The Magarima District Development Authority [DDA] says the project will power the district station and surrounding communities, providing a much-needed boost to health, education, and business services.
item.content:encoded:
Electricity is set to be restored at Magarima Station in the Magarima District of Hela Province, with major work now underway to install two new 500 kilowatt generators.

The Magarima District Development Authority [DDA] says the project will power the district station and surrounding communities, providing a much-needed boost to health, education, and business services.

Magarima DDA chief executive officer Simon Olaija confirmed to NBC News that contractor Olympus Projects Ltd is currently installing the two generators, which together will deliver 1MW of power.

"Olympus Projects Ltd is in the process of installing the generators. They have already ordered step-up transformers and we are now awaiting their arrival," he said.

"Once the transformers arrive, they will connect to the main electricity line for further inspection and approval certification by PNG Power Ltd."

Olaija said a fuel depot will also be constructed at the generator shed. The two generators will operate on a rotational basis - one during the day and the other at night - to ensure continuous power supply to the station.

The CEO explained that the DDA had previously invested significant funds in a rural electrification rollout before Magarima separated from Komo-Hulia district. Power poles were erected from Hulia LLG all the way to Magarima.

However, much of that work was destroyed.

"Most of the poles were erected near the road corridor and when work on the Mendi-Tari road sealing commenced, the poles had to be removed," Olaija said.

"The contractor engaged for the electrification project had put them within 40 meters of the road. Others were also damaged by fallen trees."

He said the loss of those poles has delayed power access for rural communities, but the new generator project will provide immediate relief to the station while long-term grid plans are reviewed.

He said restoring electricity is critical for development in the district.

"Electricity is one important service that will give rise to SME and agricultural activities. Health facilities and schools also depend on daily electricity to operate effectively," he said.

Workers from Olympus Projects Ltd on site have confirmed that installation work is progressing well.

Once the transformers arrive and PNG Power completes its inspection, Magarima Station and nearby areas will be reconnected to power for the first time in years.

item.title: Western targets 35pc child vaccination rate
item.description: The Western Provincial Health Authority [WPHA] will roll out a province-wide catch-up immunisation campaign next month to address low vaccination rates among infants. Recent health data revealed that only 35 per cent of the estimated 15,300 children under one year old in Western are fully vaccinated.
item.content:encoded:
The Western Provincial Health Authority [WPHA] will roll out a province-wide catch-up immunisation campaign next month to address low vaccination rates among infants.

Recent health data revealed that only 35 per cent of the estimated 15,300 children under one year old in Western are fully vaccinated.

The campaign will target children who missed routine doses to guard against potential outbreaks of preventable childhood illnesses.

WPHA patrol teams will conduct field visits in North Fly and Middle Fly districts from Aug 17 to 28, before moving to South Fly and Delta Fly districts from Sept 7 to 18.

Officials clarified that the upcoming exercise is a routine immunisation drive rather than an emergency outbreak response like last year’s polio campaign.

The vaccines will follow the standard routine schedule given at one month, two months, three months, six months, and nine months.

WPHA said geographical accessibility and logistical barriers contributed significantly to children missing their scheduled shots.

As part of the outreach, health teams will conduct field surveys to gather data on service barriers and improve future health delivery.

WPHA urged parents and caregivers to bring their child health record books when teams visit their villages.

"The best protection any parent can give their children is to have them vaccinated. Vaccines are safe," WPHA said in a statement.

Resources have been allocated to ensure field teams reach remote communities.

Parents are advised to consult their nearest health facility or the WPHA office in Daru for details.

item.title: Port Moresby grid hit by 75% power drop as PNG Power turns to load shedding
item.description: PNG Power Limited [PPL] is currently generating only 25 per cent of the electricity required to supply its primary grid in Port Moresby and the Central province, triggering widespread blackouts across the region. The state-owned power utility has been forced to implement continuous load shedding as a safety measure during an extended dry season.
item.content:encoded:
PNG Power Limited [PPL] is currently generating only 25 per cent of the electricity required to supply its primary grid in Port Moresby and the Central province, triggering widespread blackouts across the region.

The state-owned power utility has been forced to implement continuous load shedding as a safety measure during an extended dry season.

The crisis was the central focus of a high-level meeting in Port Moresby on Tuesday between the PPL chief executive officer and the Minister for International Trade and Investment, Richard Maru.

Discussions focused on dry-season energy security for the National Capital District (NCD) and Central amidst ongoing El Niño weather conditions.

Speaking after the meeting, Maru revealed that severe reductions in water levels at major hydroelectric dams were directly responsible for the current load shedding.

Due to prolonged low rainfall, both the Rouna and Edevu hydro schemes have been forced to scale back generation significantly.

The Edevu Hydro Power Plant, which has a 54-megawatt [MW] capacity, is currently producing just 14MW.

As a result, power grid stability now relies heavily on independent power producers, namely NiuPower and Dirio, to cover the shortfall.

Maru said he intends to take a submission to Cabinet this week to seek approval for a supplementary budget to fund emergency dry-season energy support for PPL.

He emphasized that reliable electricity supply to the NCD and Central underpins critical operations, including hospitals, schools, water and sanitation services, public safety, and general commerce.

He added that maintaining supply through the dry season directly protects these vital services and aligns with the National Government’s overall electrification objectives.

Meanwhile, a major 25MW solar power project in Wawin, Morobe, will be officially announced next week.

Maru said the 25MW of power will supply the Ramu Grid for the next five months to replace reliance on the privately operated Munum Power Station, which has been causing PPL substantial financial losses.

item.title: Water PNG announces emergency water rationing in Lorengau
item.description: Water PNG has announced emergency water rationing in Lorengau, Manus, following a significant decline in surface water levels caused by the prolonged dry season. In a public notice issued on Tuesday, the company stated that the surface water intake had fallen to critically low levels, resulting in insufficient raw water entering its treatment system.
item.content:encoded:
Water PNG has announced emergency water rationing in Lorengau, Manus, following a significant decline in surface water levels caused by the prolonged dry season.

In a public notice issued on Tuesday, the company stated that the surface water intake had fallen to critically low levels, resulting in insufficient raw water entering its treatment system.

According to Water PNG, the low water level is also causing the suction pit to draw air, forcing raw water transfer pumps to repeatedly switch on and off and disrupting normal water production.

The company advised that customers across Lorengau will experience intermittent water supply while the emergency water rationing remains in effect.

Water PNG confirmed that its technical team will conduct an urgent inspection of the water source to assess current conditions and identify both short-term and long-term solutions to improve water supply.

The utility is urging households, businesses, schools, health facilities and government departments to use water responsibly by storing enough for essential needs, prioritising drinking, cooking, sanitation and hygiene, and reporting any water leaks or illegal connections.

Water PNG added that the emergency water rationing will remain in place while assessments continue, with further updates to be provided as more information becomes available.

item.title: 23 children among 58 displaced SARV victims
item.description: A total of 23 children are among 58 victims displaced by Sorcery Accusation-Related Violence [SARV] who have received essential food, accommodation, and logistical assistance from the PNG Tribal Foundation to attend court hearings in Kundiawa and Port Moresby.

item.title: IPA, Santos sign MoU to strengthen landowner companies and SMEs
item.description: The Investment Promotion Authority [IPA] has signed a Memorandum of Understanding [MoU] with Santos Limited to design and deliver training programs aimed at boosting compliance and corporate governance for landowner companies and small businesses in resource areas.
